channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: India: Rising inflation pressures challenge RBI – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kunal Kundu notes that India’s September Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose to 5.54% year-on-year, with food inflation at 7.74% and core inflation at 4.2%, signalling broadening price pressures.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Trade détente and PBoC fix support Yuan – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts highlight that Beijing’s new trade agreement with Brussels, alongside a US–China tariff framework, modestly improves China’s external backdrop. They note the PBoC’s USD/CNY fixing model points to a slightly stronger Yuan and that both USD-CNY and USD-CNH fell to 6.69 last week, as easing trade tensions reduce headwinds for China’s export sector and current account.

item.title: Gold fails to sustain a break above $4,200, US CPI in focus
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates losses on Monday after reversing earlier gains as traders avoid taking large positions ahead of US inflation data due later this week, which could offer fresh cues on the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) next move.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Daily chart favours bulls despite mixed momentum signals
item.description: USD/CHF starts the week on a positive note, snapping a two-day losing streak as broad US Dollar (USD) strength and a wide interest rate differential between the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Swiss National Bank (SNB) keep the Swiss Franc (CHF) under persistent selling pressure.

item.title: Australian Dollar retreats as Fed hawkish stance, Iran tensions boost US Dollar
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.6965 on Monday, down 0.24% at the time of writing after giving up its earlier gains.

item.title: Germany: AI boom versus growth drag – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Robin Winkler reviews Germany’s consensus outlook, where GDP growth is seen near 1% in 2027 before sliding towards 0% by 2030 as demographics weigh on potential growth.

item.title: Euro remains on the back foot amid French debt concerns
item.description: EUR/USD gives up earlier gains on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) remains firmly bid across the board, while French political and fiscal uncertainty weighs on the Euro (EUR). At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1178, retreating from an intraday high of 1.1217.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Steepening curve and carry risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Molly Schwartz and Christian Lawrence discuss Mexico’s rates outlook after Banxico held the overnight rate at 6.50%. They note upside risks to inflation, market pricing for more than 100bp of hikes over a year, a pronounced steepening of the Mexican yield curve versus the US, and resilient foreign ownership of Mbonos and Cetes.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar retreats toward 17-month low on Oil-driven risk aversion
item.description: NZD/USD declines by 0.23% on Monday, trading around 0.5600 at the time of writing, as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: US Dollar: Geopolitics support extends gains – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that the Dollar stays well supported as markets focus on solid US growth, above-target inflation and expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening. A potentially strong US September CPI is seen keeping rate expectations elevated. Turner highlights DXY consolidation above 102 as bullish and prefers a move towards 102.85 this week, with geopolitics offering additional support.

item.title: Canadian Dollar struggles as Fed and BoC policy outlooks diverge
item.description: USD/CAD trims part of its earlier decline on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) regains ground after opening the week lower. The Canadian Dollar (CAD) struggles to attract buyers as differing monetary policy expectations for the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Canada (BoC) favour the Greenback.

item.title: 0.8447 under pressure: EUR/GBP tests 16-month lows with France in the spotlight
item.description: The Euro (EUR) has resumed its broader bearish trend against the British Pound (GBP) on Monday after a mild recovery attempt at the end of last week.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Policy path steady with cautious inflation stance – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Robert Both and Emma Lawrence expect the Bank of Canada (BoC) to keep the Overnight Rate at 2.25% through 2026, before lifting it back to a neutral 2.75% in 2027.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains significantly on fresh RBI measures
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades significantly higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday. The USD/INR pair falls 1% to near 95.80 as the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) fresh measures to curb US Dollar demand have brought relief for the Indian currency.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar approaches YTD lows amid a subdued risk appetite
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) retraces previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday and turns negative on the daily chart, with markets cautious amid the growing tensions in the Middle East and Oil prices at high levels.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Mixed outlook against Euro around French spread moves – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING says EUR/CHF is consolidating after a sharp fall driven by French debt concerns that dampened ECB tightening expectations. Markets still price further rate hikes, and ING sees it as too early to cancel 2027 ECB hikes. The bank flags a possible correction to 0.9230/0.9250, while calmer periods could see EUR/CHF trade back to 0.9350/0.9400.

item.title: US Dollar: Consolidation at higher levels before CPI – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the Dollar index is holding just above 102.00 as softer US data and cautious Federal Reserve (Fed) communication have reduced expectations for immediate rate hikes. Markets now price only modest tightening this month.

item.title: British Pound erases early gains against US Dollar, US CPI in focus
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) gives back its early gains against the US Dollar (USD), trading flat at around 1.3235 during the European session on Monday.

item.title: WTI rebounds as Middle East tensions clash with Russia-Ukraine peace hopes
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil rises by 1.00% on Monday, trading around $91.90 at the time of writing. Crude Oil prices are supported by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, despite prospects of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine that could ease supply concerns.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Pound extends gains, nearing 210.00 amid Yen weakness
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) extends gains for the second consecutive day on Monday, as concerns about the high Japanese public debt and rising Oil prices keep the Japanese Yen (JPY) on its back foot.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Firmer tone but capped at 0.7000 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD closed firmly around 0.6981, with underlying momentum continuing to improve. For today, they expect the pair to edge higher but see resistance at 0.7000, with support at 0.6970 and 0.6960.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI measures support INR against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Santosh Ejanthkar and Tanmay Purohit highlight that USD/INR fell by more than 1% after the RBI unveiled a broad FX-support package, including a dedicated oil import window and tighter restrictions on corporate hedging.

item.title: Swiss Franc dips as geopolitical tensions and Oil prices boost the US Dollar
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) has turned lower on Monday and is retracing gains from the previous two trading days against the US Dollar, as tensions in the Middle East and a highly likely failure of the Russia-Ukraine ceasefire deal are dampening risk appetite.

item.title: CEE FX: Inflation data versus global Dollar strength – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky highlights a busy week for CEE with key inflation releases and IMF meetings, while regional FX remains driven mainly by global factors.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $60.69 per troy ounce, down 0.22% from the $60.83 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Euro holds range vs Yen as French strains, Japan’s loose policy offset
item.description: EUR/JPY trades without a clear direction on Monday, hovering around 177.35 at the time of writing, posting a modest daily gain of 0.04%.

item.title: Japanese Yen seems vulnerable vs bullish amid fiscal woes, Mideast jitters
item.description: The USD/JPY pair attracts buyers for the second straight day, though it lacks strong follow-through and trades below mid-158.00s during the first half of the European session on Monday.

item.title: S&P 500: Earnings strength offsets yield headwinds – HSBC
item.description: HSBC Asset Management notes that global equities, including the S&P 500, have shown resilience as the index inches toward the 8000 level despite high Oil prices, a hawkish Federal Reserve and surging bond yields.

item.title: Euro falls against Canadian Dollar amid French debt crisis
item.description: EUR/CAD inches lower after posting modest gains in the previous day, trading around 1.5960 during European hours on Monday.

item.title: Gold sticks to modest losses, seems vulnerable below $4,200 on Fed hike bets, bullish USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its intraday retracement slide from a one-week high, hitting a fresh daily low around $4,170 during the early European session on Monday.
